text: They lured travellers off the road with a story of a wounded friend, and killed each one who followed.
They killed the guards of a caravan in their sleep and drove off its pack animals.
They killed a shopkeeper over a debt of a few cats, and left the body in the shop for the customers to find.
They killed a bounty hunter who came for them, and hung the body at a crossroads as a warning to the next one.
They left a trail of dead travellers along a trade route, each one stripped of every cat and every scrap of armour.
They killed a camp of miners for the ore in their packs.
They cut down a farmer and the whole household when the farm would not hand over its harvest.
They poisoned the water barrels of a roadside camp, and robbed the dead the next morning.
They took travellers from the road at night and sold them to slavers.
They kidnapped a merchant, and sent the ransom demand with a lock of the merchant's hair.
They seized a work crew at a mine and kept the workers in chains until the owners paid.
They captured the scout of a patrol and held the scout for ransom.
They set fire to the fields of a farming outpost on the night before the harvest.
They burned a trade post to the ground with its traders still barred inside.
They wrecked the wells and the water pumps of an outpost, so its people had to leave or go thirsty.
They smashed the mining gear of an outpost and set its stores alight.
They led a raid on a town gate and set the guard post on fire.
They stirred up a crowd of labourers into a riot that burned half a market.
They beat a gate guard senseless and walked into town with the guard's own weapon.
They broke both arms of a debt collector and sent the collector home with nothing.
They ambushed a patrol on the road and left its members bleeding in the sand.
They started a bar brawl that left three town guards unable to stand.
They ambushed the escort of a high official on the road, and wounded the official before the guards drove them off.
They forced their way into a wealthy household and beat its head in front of the servants.
They attacked an officer of the law in the open street, in front of the officer's own men.
They robbed a trade caravan of its whole cargo and sold it off piece by piece in the bars.
They broke into a storehouse and carried off a season's worth of trade goods.
They ran a long con of false debts and forged deeds, and vanished with the savings of a dozen families.
They held up travellers on a trade route for a toll of their own invention, and beat anyone who could not pay.
They posed as an official, collected fees from a whole town, and fled with the cats.
They emptied the armoury of a guard post and sold the weapons to bandits.
